abstract: We prove that exact decision-$\mathsf{SVP}$ in the coefficient $\ell_\infty$-norm is $\mathsf{NP}$-complete for principal ideals and free modules of rank two over the cyclotomic rings $R_n=\mathbb{Z}[X]/(X^n+1)$, where $n$ ranges over powers of two. For each case, we give a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction from the Subset Sum problem. For an instance with $s$ positive input integers, the output lattice has dimension $O(s)$. A solution to the original Subset Sum instance can be recovered in polynomial time from any nonzero output lattice vector of norm at most the specified bound. We also transfer these reductions from $R_n$ to the power-of-two cyclic rings $S_{2n}=\mathbb{Z}[X]/(X^{2n}-1)$. This gives $\mathsf{NP}$-completeness of decision-$\mathsf{SVP}$ in the coefficient $\ell_\infty$-norm for principal ideals and free modules of any fixed positive rank over these rings.
hook: Finding the shortest vector in some structured lattices is NP-complete, even for ideals in cyclotomic rings.
hook_turn: even for ideals in cyclotomic rings.
summary: The authors prove exact shortest-vector decision in the l-infinity norm is NP-complete for principal ideals and rank-two modules over power-of-two cyclotomic rings, by reduction from Subset Sum. It extends to any fixed rank over related cyclic rings. This concerns exact worst-case hardness, not the approximate problems that cryptographic schemes rely on.
title: $\mathsf{SVP}_\infty$ Is NP-Hard for Power-of-two Cyclotomic Ideals
